chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said: I come to the Imam while he had preceded me by one rak'ah in the fajr prayer. Then when he gave salām, it occurred in my heart that I had completed [the prayer], so I remained remembering Allah until the sun rose. When the sun rose, I stood up, and then remembered that the Imam had indeed preceded me by one rak'ah. He عليه السلام said: “If you are still in your place, then complete it with one rak'ah; but if you have already departed, then you must repeat [the prayer].”

His statement عليه السلام, “but if you have already departed, then you must repeat [the prayer],” means by that when he has turned his back to the qiblah. And his statement عليه السلام in the first report, “he went and came back,” is understood in a different way: that he went and came back without turning his back to the qiblah. What he narrated indicates that.

key_terms.اسْتَدْبَرَ الْقِبْلَةَ: Turning one's back to the qiblah, which affects the ruling.
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The prayer leader whom the person joined after missing one rak'ah.
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: The fajr prayer, whose missed rak'ah is the subject of this ruling.
key_terms.انْصَرَفْتَ: Having departed from one's place after the prayer.
key_terms.ذَاكِرًا لِلَّهِ: Engaged in dhikr, remembering Allah while remaining seated.
key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: A unit of salat (prayer) that was missed and must be completed.

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets to complete a missed rak'ah in fajr prayer until after sunrise, should he complete it or repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who joined the fajr prayer late behind the Imam and then forgot to complete the missed rak'ah until after sunrise. The ruling given is that if he is still in his place, he completes the missing rak'ah, but if he has already departed in a manner involving turning away from the qiblah, he must repeat the prayer.
